title: Each change lands as one typed squash commit
statement: Each change MUST land on main as one squash commit whose title opens with a Conventional Commits type, type(scope)!: summary, the type one of feat, fix, perf, refactor, docs, test, build, ci, chore, revert or spec (a change to the spec's records alone), the scope optional and lowercase, and ! for a breaking change, so each release's notes group themselves; its body lists the branch's commit subjects. Commits on a branch MAY be free-form. lathe/scripts/check-commits.ts checks the title: the commit-msg hook on main, scripts/ci.sh --title before the merge, and the PR title check on GitHub.

title: A schema change is a numbered migration, read on the next load
statement: A change to Lathe's schema MUST be the next numbered migration, which takes effect on the next load and is checked against every product's data; the server and the aggregates' commands MUST NOT change the schema.

title: Types, the reference and the registry come from the schema
statement: The record types, the reference and the registry of kinds, relations, obligations and link roles MUST be written from the schema and never by hand, and the schema MUST describe every table, column, kind and relation.

title: A breaking schema change raises the version and brings a converter
statement: A schema change that data already written may not pass MUST raise the schema version in schema/version.json and bring the converter that moves a product's data forward one version.

title: Each record is one line of its kind's data file
statement: Each record MUST be one row of its kind's table and one line of its data file, a JSON object with its columns in table order, and a file MUST go when its last row goes.

title: Line and field order change nothing
statement: The order of a data file's lines and of each line's fields MUST NOT change what the data means, and the same rows MUST be written as the same bytes whatever order they were written in.

title: Each test sits under what it tests
statement: Each test MUST be of the test kind named after what it tests or its owner, and sit under that one record, the only obligation it proves.

title: Nothing the Reader is looking at jumps
statement: As the Reader opens views, moves around, resizes and reloads, in any use case, nothing they are looking at MUST move unless they moved it.

title: Big maps stay smooth
statement: On a product of about ten times Lathe's records, the Graph, the ERD and the Trace MUST pan and zoom with no frame over 20 ms (60 frames a second), the arrow walk MUST frame a new focus within 200 ms, and each map MUST be laid out off the main thread (the Graph's within 4 s) and again only when what it reads changes, the map before it staying visible and answering the camera, so panning keeps 60 frames a second through a reload.

title: The spec reads on a phone
statement: On a phone, the Reader MUST be able to find a record, read it, switch its view and move between views, with text they can read and targets sized for a finger, and on a tablet keep the Workbench with targets sized for a finger.

title: Every view and control works by keyboard and assistive technology
statement: Every view and control MUST be usable by keyboard and assistive technology, at WCAG 2.2 AA.

title: Every command runs from the keyboard
statement: The Reader MUST be able to reach and run every command of the app from the keyboard, by its VS Code key or from the palette, and hear what it changed.

title: A shortcut is learned where it is used
statement: Wherever a command can be run, the Reader MUST be able to learn its keys there: in its tooltip, the palette, the shortcuts sheet and through assistive technology, all from one keymap.

title: The window works under Lathe's own title bar
statement: In a Product window, the Reader MUST be able to go back and forward, open quick find, toggle the panels and move the window from Lathe's own title bar, which follows the theme.

title: A menu choice runs the same command as its key
statement: The menu bar MUST have File, Edit, View, Window and Help, and choosing an item that stands for one of the Workbench's commands MUST run that command by its ID, as its key would; the Workbench MUST know when it runs in a Product window, and nowhere else.

title: A second launch goes to the running app
statement: The app MUST run as one instance: a second launch, or a folder opened through Finder or the Dock, MUST open that folder's window in the running app, or bring it forward when it is open.

title: The window behaves like a native one
statement: The window MUST NOT check spelling, MUST use overlay scroll bars and native context menus (Cut, Copy and Paste on text), and MUST reopen in full-window mode when it was closed in full-window mode. In full-window mode on macOS the title bar MUST drop the room it keeps for the hidden traffic lights.

title: macOS keeps no window state for Lathe
statement: The app MUST opt out of macOS window restoration, since it reopens its own windows, so a run that was killed leaves macOS nothing to offer to reopen.

title: Lathe sits in the Dock and the app menu as a Mac app does
statement: Lathe's Dock icon MUST read at every size, its Dock badge MUST count the check errors the window in front reports, and its Dock menu MUST open another folder and list the recent ones; About Lathe MUST show the versions that run and Settings… MUST open Appearance; and a folder the engine cannot load MUST open an error view that says why, with a way on.

title: On a phone nothing is cut off, overlapping, unreachable or too small to tap
statement: On a phone, upright or on its side, a page MUST NOT scroll sideways, text MUST NOT be cut off unless it ends in an ellipsis with its whole text as its title or name, and every target MUST be at least 44 × 44 px (a link inside a sentence excepted), clear of every other target and of fixed bars, and reachable by scrolling.

title: Aggregates are small
statement: An aggregate MUST be the smallest cluster of entities that must stay consistent after one command: most hold a root and a few children, and none SHOULD hold more than the product's `max_entities_per_aggregate` setting (7 by default), which `aggregate-too-large` enforces. A rule that spans two aggregates MUST be a specification a command checks, or follow through an event and a policy.

title: A query reads only its read model
statement: A query MUST read only its own read model, never a repository or an aggregate's model. A read model MUST have a shape of its own, built by its projection from the data or the events it hears, and its query handler answers from that shape alone.

title: Definitions build up, never in a circle
statement: A term MUST be defined only by plain words and terms defined below it, and MUST name each term its meaning uses with a builds_on link; no term MAY build on itself through any chain of links, which the Domain aggregate refuses (term-builds-on-itself). A meaning that uses another term's title as a whole word, in any letter case, singular or plural, without a builds_on link to it is a warning (term-used-unlinked); text in backticks is code and does not count. Every glossary MUST list terms bottom-up: each after everything it builds on, otherwise by title.

title: An outcome is a change someone would miss
statement: A business outcome MUST be a change in the world for the product's users, not a property of the product or of how it is built (those are standard or pattern rules); it MUST state its measure and a target by a date, and MUST be measured by its tests or records, or measured outside the code (measured_outside) when they can't. Everything else in the product MUST serve at least one outcome. The test: if the product disappeared, would someone notice this outcome was lost? The serves-no-outcome warning names each aggregate, read model or obligation no outcome reaches, outcome-target-undated each target with no date, and the outcome-not-measured gap each outcome nothing measures.

title: A record nests in its parent only as its composition
statement: Where a view draws records inside other records, a record MUST nest in its parent only when it cannot exist without it and belongs wholly to it, its composition: an aggregate's entities and the commands under them, a use case's UC requirements and flows, a flow's steps, a journey's steps, a pattern's and a standard's rules, a value object's constraints, a read model's queries, projection and reader, an endpoint's API requirements, a view's view requirements, and each record's tests. Every other relation, a record's parent included (a use case in its domain, an invariant or a domain event in its aggregate, a policy under its command, a technical record under what it implements), MUST be drawn as a link, not as holding. The Graph's Map layout (`LA-EXP-DS12`) holds to it.

title: A use case is one role's command or query and the steps to it
statement: A use case MUST be one role invoking one command, or asking one query, with the steps that lead to it. That operation is its result: a command for a command use case, a query for a query use case, the kind following from the result and never stored. No two use cases of a product MAY share their first actor and their result (use-case-identity-taken). A command use case's flow MUST invoke no command but its result, on any path, through any interface and whoever the step's subject is. Its other steps only ask queries or invoke nothing (use-case-invokes-another-command). A second command is a second use case, strung to the first in a journey when one waits on the other, or the command of a policy when the product does it on its own. A query use case MUST invoke no command, and is anchored on its query, never on the read model, which serves several questions. A use case is done when its result is invoked: through each interface that offers it, its main path MUST invoke its result (use-case-result-not-invoked). A command use case MAY ask queries after its result, such as one confirming it; a query use case's main path MUST end in its result, its last step that invokes anything asking it (use-case-not-done). A command use case's title MUST start with its command's verb (Borrow a tool for Borrow a tool), which use-case-title-off-result warns of. A query use case is titled for the question, with a verb of its own (See the tools waiting for repair). A quality, a property every use case keeps such as nothing jumping or working by keyboard, results in no operation and MUST NOT be a use case: it is a standard rule the use cases meet. Which operation is a use case's result is the one judgment left.

title: A record's product and domain come from its parents
statement: Each record MUST take its product and domain from its parent, and a record with no owner MUST belong to the one domain that uses it, or be shared when two or none do.

title: An ID is used once, fits its scope and has one known parent
statement: A record MUST have an ID no other record has, starting with its parent's or domain's ID, and one parent that names a record; data that breaks this MUST end the load with one data-refused error per refusal.

title: Records relate only through links the schema allows
statement: Two records MUST be related only by a link of a relation the schema allows between their kinds, and only when they belong to one product; a link or parent the schema does not allow MUST end the load with a data-refused error.

title: An ID in text is plain text
statement: An ID a record names in its text MUST be kept as written and MUST NOT make a link, and no check MUST read text for IDs.

title: A use case sits with its result
statement: A use case MUST sit in its result's domain (use-case-result-in-domain), with its result's aggregate for a command use case or its read model for a query use case, worked out from the result and never stored. The aggregates and read models MUST name the business outcomes their use cases are for (use-case-group-serves-no-outcome), and every outcome MUST be served by one (outcome-not-served).

title: A use case is named for its result, a journey for its goal
statement: A use case's title MUST name what its actor does, verb first, with a qualifier only when needed: a command use case's title starts with its command's verb (Borrow a tool, for the command Borrow a tool), which use-case-title-off-result warns of, and a query use case's names the question, with a verb of its own (See the tools waiting for repair). It MUST NOT name an interface or mechanism (a command line, a window, a page, a layer of code): interfaces belong to its flows. It SHOULD be two to six words. A journey's title MUST name the one goal its steps reach together, from its trigger to its result, verb first (Get a damaged tool back in lending), naming no interface, holding no list and using the domain's own verb: Create, Read, Update, Delete, Change or Edit MAY be used only as the domain's own word for its goal, never over a record or data. title-breaks-convention warns of a use case or journey title that holds one of its product's interface titles or an interface word, and of a journey title that holds a list or a CRUD verb over a record or data.

title: Every title is sentence case, unique and without a period
statement: Every record's title MUST be in sentence case, MUST be unique within its kind and product, and MUST NOT end with a period; detail goes in its statement or description. Its length SHOULD fit its family: a name one to four words, a goal two to six, a statement one short sentence of about fifteen words. The store refuses a title another record of its kind and product has, compared trimmed (and in any letter case, except a code-bound kind's identifiers, which compare exactly), with `title-unique`, and one ending with a period with `title-period`. Two rules MAY share a title when they also share a file: one function in code can enforce two invariants, and each invariant keeps its own rule, so the function is not split for the record's sake.

title: A name is a noun phrase with no article
statement: A product, integration and interface MUST be titled by its proper name (Tool Library, Git, Self-service kiosk). A domain MUST be a noun for a business area or ability (Lending, Invoice management). An aggregate, entity, value object, term, read model, pattern and standard MUST be a singular noun phrase with no article (Loan, Record ID, Loan history); a domain service a noun phrase for what it works out (Due date, Next ID); a view its subject and form (Loan page, Return dialog); a UI component a noun phrase for what it shows (Record card); a test data set a noun phrase for its contents (Complete example library); and a business outcome the state wanted, as a noun phrase (More tools in use). A name SHOULD be one to four words.

title: A goal starts with its verb
statement: A use case, command and skill MUST be titled by an imperative verb and its object (Borrow a tool). A query MUST start with Get, List or Find and name what it returns (List overdue loans), which `query-title-verb` warns of. A flow MUST be titled as its use case (Borrow a tool), which `flow-title-off-pattern` warns of. A goal SHOULD be two to six words.

title: A happening says what happened or follows
statement: A domain event MUST be a past participle phrase, subject first (Tool borrowed), which `event-tense` warns of. A policy MUST read "When" its event, then its reaction (When a tool is returned damaged, hold it for repair). A flow step MUST name the actor or system and what it does, in the present tense (The member picks a tool).

title: A statement is true when its rule holds
statement: An invariant, constraint, UC, view and API requirement, standard rule and pattern rule MUST be titled by a short sentence that is true when the rule holds (A loan has one borrower). A specification MUST be a yes/no condition with no article (Tool is available), which `specification-title-article` warns of. Every test MUST be titled by the observable result it shows (An overdue loan is refused a renewal), never "Tests that…" or "Should…", which `test-title-not-a-result` warns of.

title: A code-bound title is the identifier in code
statement: A data model, projection, command, query, event and endpoint handler, service, repository, adapter, predicate, value type, rule (by the name its refusal carries, such as `step-fulfills-own-use-case`), table, event type, and a product's code-bound kinds (such as an API client, shared module, entry point, tooling, IPC channel or plugin hook) MUST be titled by the identifier exactly as in code, with no whitespace (`LoanRow`, `buildReference`, `loan`); how it works goes in its description, where its kind has one. An endpoint MUST be its method and address, a command-line command its invocation (lathe use-case add-flow-step), and a check the kebab-case name of the mistake (event-tense). The store refuses a title out of its kind's form (meta_kind_title, which a product kind gives as its title_form) with `title-form`, and an endpoint titled other than by its method and address with the endpoint table's CHECK.

title: Every kind's text is required or absent
statement: Every kind MUST have at most one lead text, the field that opens its page: statement for something that must hold, goal for a use case, meaning for a term, field or setting, description for a thing that is. A lead MUST be required (NOT NULL and never blank), and MUST say what the title, the parent, the links and the facts cannot, never restating another record. A kind whose record only implements another in the domain layer (data model, value type, predicate, event type, service) and a flow, flow step or table have none. A test's scenario MUST give When and Then, with any setup opening its When; its shared starting state is the test data set it starts from. A product kind's lead is a field named statement, goal, meaning or description: at most one, and required, or the store refuses the declaration (`product-kind`).

title: Mistakes are refused, not found
statement: Lathe MUST refuse data and changes that break its model when they are made, not report them afterwards; a rule that can be enforced when something is written MUST be enforced then (poka-yoke: make illegal states unrepresentable).

title: One way to do each thing
statement: Lathe MUST offer one way to do each thing (standard work: one obvious way): one command for each intent on an aggregate, each rule written once, in the code of what it governs, and each interface naming the one command it runs.

title: No exceptions
statement: Every rule MUST hold everywhere it applies, with no exception, waiver, exemption or recorded deviation. Where a rule does not fit a case, the model or the code MUST change until the case meets it, or the rule MUST change everywhere at once (LA-STD-PRINCIPLES-R04).

title: Change the standard, not the instance
statement: When the standard way proves wrong, it MUST be changed everywhere at once (a hard cutover, with no aliases or old forms kept), not worked around in one place; what no longer serves a purpose MUST be removed.

title: Essential complexity is decided once, per product
statement: Every essential record (a business outcome, the domain model, a use case or pattern, the what of interface design, the API requirements of a public API, a quality standard) MUST be decided once, in its own product and in its people's words: it MUST serve one of the product's business outcomes, and it MUST NOT name how the product is built in ways its kind has no business with (a technical kind, a mechanism of an interface or of storage, one of the product's interfaces, or a word the product lists as technology; a view may name its page, a flow its interface). Whether a record is essential MUST be its kind's, never a label on the record: a kind that would hold both is split.

title: Accidental complexity is derived, provided, or a recorded fill at a slot
statement: Every accidental record of the technical specification MUST be derived (a tooling record generates it), provided (something outside the product provides it, or the record it sits under), or a fill: written by hand at a pattern's slot, against the slot's contract, and serving an essential record: the one it sits under, the obligation it builds, the aggregate it persists, one a product relation links it to in either direction, or one that sits under it. An engineering standard and its rules are the rules that code follows, not code, so they fill no slot: each MUST be provided, or followed, a rule when a record accounted for in one of those ways meets it and a standard when one of its rules is followed. Each fill MUST be counted as accidental debt, and three fills of one slot MUST be reported as a pattern candidate, unless the slot says, with a reason that is never empty, that its fills vary by design because each is its own record's business logic; the slot's page MUST then show that reason.

title: What Lathe publishes names no client, person or machine
statement: Everything Lathe publishes, its code, specs, tests, examples and docs, MUST NOT name a product Lathe was tried on for a client or a collaborator, a person as a person, or one machine's own folders (a person's home folder or the system's temporary folder). A spec names roles (Owner, Reader, Agent), an example names the idea itself, and a test that needs a home folder uses the made-up person `person`; only the packages' author and owner, Lathe's package name and the owner of its public repository name the author. Working notes that name a product, a person or a machine are kept apart from what is published.

title: Main is wholly traced and clean
statement: On every merge into main, `lathe check` on Lathe's own spec and the Tool Library MUST count 100% of their obligations designed, built and proved, summed over every domain, and MUST print 0 errors and 0 warnings; a merge that misses either MUST NOT land.

title: A technical record names its helper files, and they count as traced
statement: A technical record whose code is split across files MUST name the other files as its helper files, each from the product root and none named twice or by another record; a helper file MUST count as traced, and the record MUST count as built only when every one of its files exists.
